_note: Joint party list of Lapid (Yesh Atid) and Bennett (Bennett 2026), running together as 'Beyachad'. Platform sourced from https://bennett2026.org.il/. Voted positions use Yesh Atid's 25th Knesset record (Bennett had no Knesset data for this term).

stated_position.source: Both parties opposed settlement expansion; security-pragmatism over ideological expansion

voted_position.source: Yesh Atid faction aggregate — Yesh Atid is one half of the Beyachad joint list; Bennett's party had no 25th-Knesset faction

stated_position.source: Yesh Atid supports two-state in principle; Bennett's 'shrinking the conflict' leaves final status open — merged platform is cautiously open

voted_position.source: Proxy vote, not the same question: the vote was on recognizing a Palestinian state (the 18 Jul 2024 resolution opposing recognition, 68-9). Parties that support two states in a peace agreement but oppose unilateral recognition voted with the resolution, so this understates their support for q02. — Manual encoding of 25th Knesset voting positions: Knesset vote July 18, 2024 — 68-9 resolution AGAINST recognizing Palestinian state. Voting FOR this resolution = AGAINST q02.

stated_position.source: be-yahad.org.il campaign platform: 'a proactive security doctrine' with 'zero containment' of threats and drafting the 20,000 additional soldiers the IDF needs, alongside regional alliances rather than endless cycles of conflict — firm on Hamas but against an open-ended war

voted_position.source: Manual encoding of 25th Knesset voting positions: No clean single vote. Inferred from Knesset coalition/opposition positions on ceasefire proposals. Coalition voted against ceasefire motions; opposition split.

stated_position.source: Both support unified Jerusalem; Bennett holds this more firmly (score 2) vs Yesh Atid open to functional arrangements (score 1)

voted_position.source: Manual encoding of 25th Knesset voting positions: No direct vote — consistent cross-party position. All Jewish parties agree, Arab parties oppose. Based on stated positions across votes.
